transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 65 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Gomez (Aurelia Head of ML), Tom Baker (Platform Eng), Li Wei (Security), Arun Shah (MLOps)

Summary:
Quick technical deep dive to align on benchmark methodology: prompt sets, load generation, apples-to-apples comparisons across hosted/dedicated/private, KV cache warmup, batching profiles, and quantization tradeoffs.

[00:00] Jasmine: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jasmine from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, we'll keep this pretty technical but the goal is align on the benchmarking plan.
[00:28] Maya: thanks, yeah we want to make sure the numbers we get back are apples-to-apples, especially since we're comparing Redwood Dedicated vs our on-prem inference cluster.
[00:46] Ravi: sure, and hi, i'm ravi, i'll own the benchmark scripts, the idea is to control for model variant, batch size, kv cache behavior, quantization level, and of course network overhead when we run VPC/on-prem.
[01:12] Tom: quick question, when you say apples-to-apples, do you include the network egress within the latency numbers or only server-side p95?
[01:28] Diego: good callout, we recommend both. server-side p50/p95/p99 without client-side network, and an end-to-end number that includes our routing + VPC hop so you can see real user impact.
[01:50] Maya: ok, that helps. also we have mixed seq lengths; our prompt distribution is skewed -- about 60% short prompts (<64 tokens) and 20% long (200-400 tokens).
[02:10] Ravi: perfect, we'll make the load generator replay that distribution. we also need to decide on KV cache warmup: whether we pre-warm cache with prefix traces or let it fill during ramp-up.
[02:30] Arun: for production it's warm, but for bench we want to measure both cold and warm starts.
[02:45] Jasmine: exact. recommended approach: baseline cold start, then steady-state with a warm KV cache and measured hit rate.
[03:02] Li Wei: security note -- if we're running on-prem, we need to validate KMS integration and key rotation, can you send the KMS integration doc?
[03:18] Diego: yes, will attach. also note that on private deployments we sometimes see slight differences because of kernel selection and CUDA/cuDNN versions, so we should record software stack details.
[03:40] Maya: good point, we run on A100s right now but driver versions vary across clusters.
[03:52] Ravi: we'll include a software stack checklist in the template.

Topics: prompt sets, load generator, sequence length distribution, batching, quantization settings (fp16, int8-ish quant), KV cache hit/miss scenarios, VPC network overhead, metrics to capture (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens).

[06:10] Tom: about quantization -- you support multiple quant pipelines, what's the recommended way to compare quality degradation vs perf?
[06:32] Diego: we recommend running a small eval set (side-by-side) to compute exact match or semantic similarity metrics plus human spot-checks for hard prompts. Also compare token-level divergence and perplexity where possible.
[06:55] Maya: can we integrate our own eval harness or do you require Redwood's eval?
[07:05] Ravi: you can run either; for apples-to-apples we'll publish a recommended eval harness (lightweight) that runs locally and on Redwood, same seeds/seeding.

[08:00] Speaker 1: there's also the batching regime, we saw different SLOs depending on whether batching was dynamic or fixed. how do you recommend setting batching for latency-sensitive vs throughput experiments?
[08:20] Diego: for latency-sensitive, use small max_batch (1-8) with aggressive preemption. for throughput, larger batch sizes and dynamic batching with target latency guardrails. we'll profile both.
[08:40] Ravi: we'll sweep batch sizes across 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 and record the p95 latency and tokens/sec.

[09:05] Maya: KV cache -- how do you simulate realistic cache hit rates?
[09:20] Ravi: we have two approaches: 1) replay user session prefixes to generate natural prefix reuse, 2) synthetic controlled hit-rate generator where you set percent hit. we'll do both.
[09:36] Arun: prefer the replay, that's closest to production.
[09:44] Ravi: agreed, but we need sample logs to build the replay. Maya, can you share anonymized session traces?
[09:53] Maya: yes, can scrub PII.

[10:10] Jasmine: let's outline metrics to capture in every run: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server), end-to-end latency (client), throughput (reqs/sec), tokens/sec, kv cache hit rate, GPU utilization, memory/CPU of host, cost estimate (if on Redwood hosted/dedicated).
[10:36] Tom: include tail-latency breakdowns and percentile of token generation time too.

[12:15] Ravi: on apples-to-apples model versioning: specify exact model commit/hash and tokenizer, and run tokenizer roundtrip checks. quantized models must be derived from the same FP16 checkpoint using the same quant tool/params.
[12:40] Diego: yes, we'll include a quantization spec: tool name, per-channel vs per-tensor, calibration dataset, clipping params.

[14:00] Maya: about VPC overhead, we need a method to isolate the pure network latency vs route time in our infra.
[14:18] Diego: capture TCP RTTs to the inference endpoint, and use an internal loopback measurement for server-only times. we'll provide a small network probe script.

[15:00] Speaker 2: any gotchas around KV cache size and eviction that change benchmarks?
[15:12] Ravi: eviction strategy can matter a lot. record cache size, entry TTL, and eviction policy. for deterministic runs, fix cache capacity or record hits/misses during run.

[17:30] Maya: quality checks for quantized models -- do you have automated tools to flag hallucination increases?
[17:45] Diego: automated semantic-sim metrics plus we recommend running targeted prompts for safety/guardrails. human review is necessary for fidelity-critical completions.

[20:05] Tom: what's the recommended load generation ramp pattern? linear rps increase or stepwise?
[20:20] Ravi: do both: a linear ramp to target then a step-stress where you step up 2x for 5 minutes to test throttling/fallbacks. include a cool-down.

[22:00] Jasmine: also note the Redwood routing fallbacks -- when Dedicated capacity is saturated we can fallback to lower-cost hosted variants. for benching, we should disable fallbacks to measure pure capacity unless you want to test graceful degradation.
[22:28] Maya: for the initial runs, disable fallbacks. later we'll run a degradation test.

[25:10] Arun: on metrics reporting, can you provide an artifact with plots for latency vs qps, batch size sweeps, and token generation heatmaps?
[25:25] Diego: yes, output will include CSVs and a jupyter notebook with plots. we'll attach the notebook and the raw logs.

[28:00] Ravi: small note about randomness: set deterministic sampling or a fixed seed for generation where possible to make outputs comparable. for stochastic sampling runs, record seeds and sampling params.

[30:15] Maya: how do you recommend measuring cost? raw GPU-hours isn't enough because kv cache and batching change per-token cost.
[30:30] Ravi: compute cost-per-1k-tokens under steady-state for each config based on GPU utilization * time + infra overhead; we'll provide cost estimator scripts for Redwood hosted and on-prem estimates.

[33:40] Tom: Can we include a smoke test that verifies token-level output equivalence between fp16 and quantized within thresholds?
[33:55] Diego: yes, the eval harness will include token-diff and semantic-sim thresholds.

[36:00] Speaker 3 (murmur): any notes on kernel selection differences between our custom runtime and open-source runtimes?
[36:15] Ravi: record kernel versions and provide the perf profile; some kernels favour long sequences and others short sequences -- that's why we run the sequence-length sweep.

[38:20] Jasmine: recap next steps and owners now.
[38:35] Ravi: i'll send the benchmark repo and template, includes: load generator (with seq-length distribution), replay tooling for kv cache, quant spec, eval harness, and plotting notebooks.
[38:50] Diego: i'll provision a test VPC env and run the first smoke baseline against your on-prem staging.
[39:05] Maya: i'll share the anonymized prompt corpus and short traffic profile.
[39:20] Li Wei: i'll review the KMS doc and confirm network constraints.

[40:00] Jasmine: timeline idea -- repo + prompt sets this week, initial baseline runs next week, on-prem run by week of 2026-05-11, then follow-up to review results 2026-05-18. does that work?
[40:26] Maya: that timeline works for us.

[41:00] Speaker 2: minor nit -- when you share scripts, please include expected hardware profiles so we can map to our A100/RTX clusters.
[41:12] Ravi: will do, GPU type, driver, CUDA, cuDNN, and OS.

[43:00] Tom: about logging and privacy -- will Redwood collect prompt contents when running hosted tests?
[43:15] Jasmine: for hosted tests we can enable redaction/anonymization; by default we don't persist prompts unless you opt in for debugging. private deployments leave data on your infra.

[46:00] Ravi: small follow-up on KV cache replay: we need session ids and prefix boundaries to simulate realistic cache behavior, not just random prefixes.
[46:20] Arun: we can provide sessionized logs with truncated IDs.

[50:00] Diego: one more perf note -- check GPU SM occupancy and memory bandwidth counters during sweeps, sometimes int8 runs shift bandwidth patterns.
[50:18] Ravi: included in the perf checklist.

[55:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone, this is very thorough.
[55:12] Jasmine: thanks all, we'll circulate notes and artifacts. final recap of action items is in the meeting notes.
[55:30] Meeting end.
